summary: The change passes. It is docs only: a new design note, docs/design/direct-main-single-commit-landing.md, plus a CHANGELOG entry and an appended decision, D178. All three files are on the expected deliverables list. The note covers everything the request asked for. It cites throughput review 20261113-190159-mapn and quotes the 2310.0 of 2342.1 figure. It designs one landing commit per job, built on fetched host main by Git::merge_tree and Git::commit_tree from the recorded base, and explains why that ends the repeated listings that inflate the stage. It labels the 5.0-minute saving an estimate and says how the next review measures it from THROUGHPUT.md. It lists five rejected alternatives, the risks with their failure paths, and migration and rollback, and it requires the implementing change to cite the review id. I used Grep to confirm that every function the note names exists in athena-git, land.rs and gh/landing.rs. The recorded fmt and clippy checks passed. The recorded cargo test failed in CI on one drain test, but that test and the whole drain unit (212 tests) pass when I run them here, and markdown-only edits cannot affect them. I found three minor problems. First, the note says `dispatched_from` supplies the base commit, but it returns the dispatch branch; the base comes from Verified::base(). Second, sections 3 and 6 disagree on whether the prediction is scored against the headline median or the first-record stage. Third, passing main as `head` to `plan` relies on preconditions the note does not spell out.
